summary: Backend regression for P0-P4 patches. 16/17 tests PASS. One CRITICAL bug found: P1 loyalty diamonds are NOT credited to customer balance when an authenticated online order is marked 'delivered' — the PUT /api/online-orders/{id}/status endpoint returns 200 silently but the customers.diamond_balance never increases and no loyalty_transactions row is written. RCA: customer_id is stored on the order doc as a Python str (cust['_id'] is overwritten to str by get_current_customer), but the awarding code in PUT /online-orders/{id}/status queries db.customers with {'_id': customer_id} (string) where the collection key is an ObjectId, so update_one matches zero documents (modified_count=0) and the credit + transaction log are silently skipped. All other P0-P4 patches verified working: business-hours endpoint, weekly_schedule persistence, closed-order block (HTTP 400), phone validators (422 + accepts 11+ digit), public /feedback, /api/reviews new fields, admin reply endpoint with email_sent flag.

critical.issue: Diamond reward never credited to customer.diamond_balance after delivery. Order has correct diamonds_earned (e.g. 50) but balance stays unchanged and no loyalty_transactions row is inserted. Root cause: customer_id stored as str on order doc, but db.customers._id is ObjectId — update_one({'_id': customer_id}) matches 0 docs. Reproduction: register a customer with valid 11-digit phone, place an authenticated /api/online-orders, then PUT status=delivered with admin token, then GET /api/loyalty/balance — balance is still 0.

POST /api/online-orders BLOCKED with HTTP 400 'closed' when weekly_schedule fully closed
POST /api/online-orders accepts valid 11-digit phone when open (24/7 BH override)
GET /api/reviews exposes admin_reply, replied_by, replied_at, is_feedback fields
POST /api/admin/reviews/{id}/reply persists admin_reply + returns email_sent flag (false, SMTP not configured — expected)
GET /api/loyalty/balance with Bearer token returns customer's diamond_balance
Diamond credit on delivery + idempotency
tests_executed.details: Expected balance to go from 0 -> 50 (diamonds_earned=50) but it stayed 0 after PUT status=delivered. Endpoint returned 200, no exception in logs, modified_count=0 because customer_id stored as str doesn't match ObjectId on customers._id.

action_items: Fix loyalty awarding in PUT /api/online-orders/{order_id}/status (server.py ~line 2551-2580): customer_id is a string on the order doc — wrap with ObjectId() before querying db.customers. Suggested change: `result = await db.customers.update_one({'_id': ObjectId(customer_id)}, {...})` and `customer = await db.customers.find_one({'_id': ObjectId(customer_id)})`. Alternatively, store the ObjectId on the order doc at create time. Add a defensive check that logs a warning when modified_count == 0 so this kind of silent failure surfaces in logs.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: PUT /online-orders/{id}/status silently swallows the loyalty failure — modified_count==0 should at minimum logger.warning. Right now the API returns success while the user's promised reward is lost.

Type drift: get_current_customer mutates cust['_id'] to a str (line 2123), then create_online_order writes that string into the order doc (line 2444) — but elsewhere the code (e.g. /admin/loyalty/adjust line 4173) uses ObjectId(...). This inconsistency is the proximate cause of the loyalty credit bug and is likely to bite other features (e.g. /online-orders/me uses {'customer_id': cust['_id']} where cust['_id'] is also string, which happens to work because both sides are strings — but the customers collection lookup is the broken case).
compute_business_hours_status doesn't support overnight hours (e.g. 18:00 -> 02:00). Acceptable for MVP but worth noting; the helper has a comment about this already.
/api/admin/reviews/{id}/reply email_sent is correctly false when SMTP unconfigured — verified.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Re-run /app/backend/tests/test_iteration4_p0p4.py after main agent fixes the loyalty ObjectId bug. Note Karachi local time at test time is 05:04 PKT (outside default 10:00-23:00), so loyalty + accept-order tests temporarily set 24/7 hours and reset on teardown. SMTP is intentionally unconfigured — email_sent=false on review reply is expected, not a bug.
rca of the issue: Order documents store customer_id = cust['_id'] where get_current_customer has already coerced cust['_id'] from ObjectId to str (server.py line 2123). The delivery handler at server.py line 2556 passes that string straight into db.customers.update_one({'_id': customer_id}, ...) — but the customers collection's _id is ObjectId, so the filter never matches, modified_count is 0, the transaction log block is skipped, and the API returns 200 with no warning. The fix is to wrap with ObjectId(customer_id) on both find_one and update_one (and ideally on the order create path as well, or alternatively keep _id as ObjectId on the cust dict and only stringify when serialising responses).
